items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: It was Prez, Clyde Hart, Doc West, and Shad Collins. It was a good band.

ctx.x: I think they probably had a few thousand and didn't follow up on it. I don't think it made any difference to them, you know. But we had a very good little band at this time. It was Prez, Clyde Hart, Doc West, and Shad Collins. It was a good band. And we recorded with Billie, but John Hammond at this time wanted to do something for Prez, you know. He had left Basie, and we were rehearsed at the Woodside for quite a while. But he wouldn't use a piano, you know, he would just use guitar and bass and drums. And at…

But I got him to come by our rehearsal, and just made Prez use him. And Prez loved him so we started using piano at this time. But originally it was just guitar, but now why Prez was forming this band was because John Hammond told him that he was going to book him, but Prez found out that John Hammond was only going to book him if he would work -- I think Billie was going to be Billie Holiday's band.

Before I joined Roy in New York as -- at the time my mother was ill, as I told you before, I would work around Chicago, and Basie's band would come through all the time. And Lester always liked to jam, and I was his -- Harold West and I was his official Chicago rhythm section. So we would just go all to the various -- go to all the various clubs and we would just play.
Is it true that all the major horn players carried their own rhythm sections for jam sessions?
